Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

zulm 0.0.0.9000

  • First development version: the package skeleton and its family conventions. The R interface follows in later stages.

  • Bundles the CPU subset of ‘ggml’ v0.26.0, built once per instruction-set level (baseline, sse42 and avx2 on x86-64, neon on arm64); the best level the CPU supports is loaded with the package, and options(zulm.variant =) forces another.

  • zulm_info() reports the bundled ‘ggml’ version, the variant loaded, and the CPU features it was built for.

  • Installing from source with ZULM_CFLAGS and ZULM_CXXFLAGS set builds one variant for the local CPU (not on Windows).

  • Parameter stores: zl_params(), zl_param() with init and type ("f32", "f16" or "bf16"), zl_param_get(), zl_param_set(), zl_param_names(), zl_param_count() and zl_param_tensor(); initialisers zl_init_normal(), zl_init_uniform(), zl_init_zeros() and zl_init_ones(), drawing from ‘zurand’ under a key derived from the parameter’s name.

  • zl_save() and zl_load() write and read stores as GGUF files, with metadata, at f32, f16 or bf16.

  • Every error inherits zulm_error and every warning zulm_warning; see ?"zulm-conditions" for the classes. Allocations are checked against getOption("zulm.max_bytes") (4 GiB by default).

  • Graphs: zl_graph() builds a graph once from an R function, zl_int() declares integer inputs, zl_forward() runs it any number of times on new inputs, and zl_graph_info() describes it.

  • Operations on tensors inside a graph: +, -, *, / with broadcasting, zl_scale(), zl_sum(), zl_sum_rows(), zl_mean_rows(), zl_cumsum(), the elementwise functions (zl_sqr() to zl_tanh(), zl_gelu()), zl_swiglu(), zl_crossprod(), zl_reshape(), zl_permute(), zl_t(), zl_cont(), zl_view(), zl_concat(), zl_pad(), zl_get_rows(), zl_where(), zl_clamp(), zl_tri(), zl_softmax() with masks, zl_causal_mask(), zl_rope() in both conventions, zl_rms_norm(), zl_layer_norm(), the losses zl_cross_entropy(), zl_mse() and zl_mae(), and zl_cast().

  • Every argument ‘ggml’ would assert on is checked first; an assertion that still happens while a graph is built is zulm_engine_error.

  • ‘ggml’’s log becomes messages of class zulm_message, at the level of options(zulm.log =) ("warn" by default).

  • Training: zl_adamw() and zl_sgd() describe optimisers; zl_trainer() prepares a graph with a loss for training through ‘ggml-opt’, with gradient accumulation and global-norm clipping (clip_norm); zl_step() trains on one batch, zl_grad() returns a parameter’s gradient, and zl_reset() clears the optimiser’s state. An operation without a gradient between a parameter and the loss is refused with zulm_unsupported_backward, naming it and its call.

  • zl_graph() and zl_trainer() collect garbage when graphs and trainers no longer referenced hold over 128 MB, which R’s collector does not see.

  • The bundled ‘ggml’ carries patches for the gradients of MEAN, SUB and DIV with broadcasting, and for gradient clipping in ‘ggml-opt’.

  • A NaN reaching zl_softmax() no longer stops R, a transposed column enters arithmetic and other kernels correctly, and graphs reserve memory as they grow rather than for the largest graph.

  • Random numbers come from ‘zurand’: zl_seed() sets the session key, zl_rng_uniform() and zl_rng_normal() draw in R, and zl_noise_uniform() and zl_noise_normal() draw inside a graph, anew at each training step. Draws do not depend on the thread count or on how a batch is split.

  • Reported losses (zl_cross_entropy(), zl_mse(), zl_mae(), from zl_step() and zl_forward()) are fixed-order sums of per-row values, so they are the same at any thread count.

  • Modules: zl_linear(), zl_embedding(), zl_norm(), zl_attention(), zl_mlp(), zl_block(), zl_adaln() and zl_time_embedding() declare their parameters in a store and return functions of tensors. They, the losses and two attention blocks in the styles of TimesFM and Toto are checked against PyTorch.

  • zl_threads() sets the number of threads for the session, capped at the available cores and at 2 while R CMD check limits cores. One persistent pool serves every computation, and is recreated in a forked process. A computation can be interrupted; it then signals zulm_interrupt.

  • safetensors: zl_safetensors_read(), zl_load_safetensors() (with a name map) and zl_save_safetensors(). PyTorch’s [out, in] weights load as c(in, out) with no transposition.

  • Half-precision weights: zl_load(keep_types = TRUE) and zl_load_safetensors() keep f16 and bf16 parameters in their type, and zl_param_names(types = TRUE) reports types. The documentation states their cost in precision.

  • State tensors: zl_state() declares a persistent tensor that graphs read through zl_param_tensor() and write with zl_state_write(); zl_state_get() and zl_state_set(), with offset, read and write it from R. States are neither trained nor saved. A key-value cache for incremental decoding is built from them.

  • zl_graph_cache() builds a graph per new set of input shapes for zl_forward(), and frees the least recently used under getOption("zulm.max_bytes").

  • zl_crossprod() accepts a transposed vector as its first argument, as zl_attention() makes for a single position.

  • zl_flash_attention() is ‘ggml’’s fused attention, forward only: it agrees with the plain form within f32 rounding, gives the same bits at any thread count, and attends over long contexts in memory linear in their length.

  • Arrow streams: zl_arrow_batches() reads record batches from ‘DuckDB’, Parquet or ‘arrow’ through ‘nanoarrow’ into batches of exactly rows rows, with missing values as errors or masks and the last batch dropped or padded; zl_step() and zl_forward() take the iterator as data, and zl_next() returns a batch as R arrays. zl_int() marks integer columns in its map.

  • The C table: inst/include/zulm.h declares zulm_api, registered as zulm_api_v1, for packages with LinkingTo: zulm. From C they run graphs built in R, write inputs, read outputs, read and write parameters and state tensors, draw from named streams under the session key, and fill inputs from an Arrow iterator. Failures are return codes with a message, never R errors.

  • Two vignettes: vignette("training") trains a small event-sequence model and samples from it; vignette("pretrained") runs an attention block exported by PyTorch from safetensors and decodes through a key-value cache in state tensors.

  • Fuzzing (tools/fuzz/) found, and this version fixes:

    • sizes, offsets and axes of 2^31 or more, or NA, reached ‘ggml’ as negative numbers; they are zulm_invalid_argument;
    • an invalid choice, such as zl_tri(x, "x"), gave an unclassed error; it is zulm_invalid_argument;
    • zl_param() allocated the initial values of a parameter larger than getOption("zulm.max_bytes") before refusing it;
    • training graphs whose gradients ‘ggml’ cannot carry back through a permutation, cross-entropy labels that depend on a parameter, and a half-precision product whose second operand needs a gradient, reached ‘ggml’ assertions; they are zulm_unsupported_backward;
    • gradient clipping stopped R with a ‘ggml’ assertion on a permuted parameter whose first dimension was 1 (patch P7);
    • a GGUF file with an invalid metadata type was undefined behaviour in ‘ggml’’s reader (patch P11).
